title: Windows full-gate roots leave a Hidden+System INetCache container.dat in the run's private profile that non-forced removal cannot delete
outcome:
Observed on Windows B, 2026-11-25, in two consecutive cleanups (Win2 runner, relay #131, #133 and the read-only inventory in #135).
- After the git worktree was removed and the ordinary subtrees deleted, the final non-forced recursive removal of the run root failed: "You do not have sufficient access rights to perform this operation or the item is hidden, system, or read only."
- Both residues are identical: 39 directories under userprofile/AppData, and two files.
- File 1: userprofile/AppData/Local/Microsoft/Windows/INetCache/IE/container.dat. 0 B, attributes Hidden+System+Archive+NotContentIndexed (8230), not ReadOnly. Its mtime falls inside the run: 00:34Z and 00:52Z.
- File 2: an ordinary StartupProfileData-NonInteractive PowerShell file (1.3-1.4 KB, Archive only).
- Affected roots: .tmp/j/b63e-r3-winb and .tmp/j/2506-full-e6d8bd3c-winb.

Likely mechanism (not yet proven): the launcher redirects the run's user profile and AppData into the run root. Some process in the run initialises the WinINet/IE cache there, which creates the Hidden+System container.dat. PowerShell's Remove-Item without -Force refuses Hidden/System items. The project rule requires non-forced removal, with forced removal only on Greg's word for the exact case. So every Windows run root will leave this residue.

Wanted:
- The cause is established: which stage or process creates the file.
- A supported cleanup leaves no residue that needs forced removal. Either the launcher removes its own private profile, including Hidden/System items it created, at the run's end, or the cleanup procedure in docs/test.md handles it.
- Residues already left on Windows B are disposed of under Greg's word.
acceptance: The creating stage or process of the Hidden+System INetCache/IE/container.dat under a Windows full-gate run's private profile is established from evidence and recorded on the item.

After a Windows full-gate run, the run's own private profile and temp directories can be removed completely by the supported non-forced cleanup documented in docs/test.md, leaving no Hidden or System residue; a Windows behaviour test or a recorded Windows run demonstrates it.
